rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-year replicated field experiment (RCBD, four replications) at BISA Ladhowal, Punjab, 2014-15 and 2015-16, comparing eight tillage/residue/irrigation treatments. Q2: Abstract and Section 3.3, Figs. 4 and 5 - irrigation water applied through the (sub)surface drip system was 48-53% lower in rice and 42-53% lower in wheat than flood irrigation (CT and ZT), measured with a water meter on the delivery pipe. Q8: Section 3.3 - authors state further studies are needed to compute the full water balance under SSDF to report real water savings; Section 3.2 - results need evaluating for other soil types, climates and irrigation availability before wider application; Conclusions - single N rate and fixed 7-day fertigation schedule used.
rows.notes: Q3: water saving rests on one method (metered irrigation applied) - no. Q4: reduced evaporation/drainage is asserted (and attributed to other studies), not measured; tensiometers were used only for scheduling - no. Q5: one site, one silt loam soil, one climate; two crops of one system - no. Q6: 70 m2 plots only; broader implications for NW India are extrapolation - no. Q7: mulch and fine-textured soil are discussed as influences (mulch effect is an interaction; soil-texture point is cited from other work), not stated as requirements from own findings - no. Q9: irrigation amounts had no replicate dispersion (all replicates received identical water); LSD bars/letter groupings for WPi and ranges across treatments are not dispersion measures - no.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-year replicated field experiment at BISA Ladhowal, Punjab, on SSDF under CA-based rice-wheat.
rows.notes: The study measures irrigation water input, grain yield, irrigation water productivity, partial factor productivity of N and net returns under SSDF versus flood irrigation. It does not measure resilience, risk reduction, yield stability under stress or any other risk-management outcome; the statement that drip is an option for a water-scarce future and groundwater depletion (Sections 3.6 and 4) is an inference from the water-saving result, not a tested effect. The water saving and NUE results are at most preconditions for the claimed resilience, so upstream is set to true.

notes: Full text appears complete (Table 1 is garbled by rotated layout but treatments are described in the text). The study is a single-site, two-year plot experiment; the context sentence on the claim row (46.7%/44.7% savings in rice-wheat-mungbean and maize-wheat-mungbean systems) does not come from this study, which reports 48-53% (rice) and 42-53% (wheat) savings in a rice-wheat system.
